_activity: Write the thesis: was servitude a good deal?
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the shipped 11.1 casefiles. Quotes are the casefile's own text.
source_document: Document 10 — Richard Frethorne to his parents, 1623 (11.1 Casefile B)
source_text: And when we are sick there is nothing to comfort us; for since I came out of the ship I never ate anything but peas, and loblollie (that is, water gruel)… we must work hard both early and late for a mess of water gruel and a mouthful of bread and beef…
prompt: Write a thesis that answers: Was indentured servitude a good deal for the servant?
checklist: Does it answer the question with a clear side?
Could somebody argue the other side?
model_response: Although indentured servants were promised food, clothing and land when their term ended, servitude was a bad deal for many of them, because servants like Richard Frethorne faced disease, hunger and fear with no way to leave.
